title: Smithfield budget board moves to require written communications in budget process
text:
← Back to the wire
Government
Smithfield budget board moves to require written communications in budget process
The board discussed adding a standalone bullet requiring formal communications be documented in writing rather than merging it with an existing provision.
The Smithfield Budget and Financial Review Board, meeting Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026, discussed adding a written-communication requirement to its proposed fiscal 2028 budget process guidelines.
THE PROPOSAL Under a section on communication protocols, a board member said communications between departments, the town manager and the board "must be timely, accurate, and transparent," and proposed adding language requiring documentation. "There's no he's that, she's that. It's it's a written communication," the member said, explaining the goal of putting things in writing.
STANDALONE BULLET The board debated whether to fold the written-communication language into an existing bullet or make it separate. One member argued for keeping it as its own point: "I think having it be standalone to call out" was preferable, and said "having it be written increases transpar" before being cut off. Another member noted the board itself sets its own rules: "we as the independent body we set the um the rules of operation."
The board did not take a formal vote recorded in the transcript specifically approving this bullet, though members appeared to agree on making the written-documentation requirement a standalone item within the guidelines.
